items.title: LEAP-Block: left bundle-branch area pacing beats RV pacing on death, HF events or BiV upgrade in AV block with preserved EF (JAMA)
items.summary: In a 14-centre Chinese randomised trial of 499 patients with AV block, LVEF of 50% or more and expected ventricular pacing above 40%, left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) lowered the 24-month risk of death, heart failure events or biventricular upgrade vs right ventricular pacing (Kaplan-Meier 5.0% vs 13.2%; HR 0.37) (JAMA, Oct 28, 2026).
bullets: Design: prospective, multicentre, randomised superiority trial at 14 Chinese hospitals; 499 patients randomised 1:1 (LBBAP 249, RVP 250), 482 in the primary analysis (mean age 67, 46% women).

Primary endpoint (all-cause death, HF events or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months): Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidence 5.0% with LBBAP vs 13.2% with RVP (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.19-0.73; P=0.004), consistent across all prespecified subgroups.
Among secondary outcomes, HF events were fewer with LBBAP (3.4% vs 11.3%); all-cause death, BiV upgrade, pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications did not differ significantly.
Feasibility: acute procedural success 97.9% vs 99.6% (P=0.22); true left bundle-branch capture was confirmed in 79.7% of LBBAP patients.

Context: adds randomised hard-outcome evidence for conduction system pacing as an alternative to RV pacing when a high pacing burden is expected; limits are a single country, few events, blinding not stated in the abstract, and some inconsistent figures in the abstract.
items.source: You L, et al. LEAP-Block. JAMA, Oct 28, 2026. doi:10.1001/jama.2026.18146
